Eliphelet
ē-lĭf´ĕ-lĕt
n. (a son of David born in Jerusalem; also one of David's mighty men)
Hebrew Eliphelet, meaning God is deliverance or God of escape. Several men carry it, including two of David's sons and a warrior in the roll of the thirty.

Biblical Definition

One bearer stands in the roll of David's mighty men: “Eliphelet the son of Ahasbai, the son of the Maachathite, Eliam the son of Ahithophel the Gilonite” (2 Samuel 23:34). The verse is worth reading twice, because the next name in it is Eliam the son of Ahithophel — and Eliam was Bathsheba's father, which makes Ahithophel her grandfather and goes some way to explaining why David's most gifted counsellor later joined Absalom's revolt. The other bearers are David's own sons, listed among those born to him in Jerusalem: “Ibhar also, and Elishama, and Eliphelet” (1 Chronicles 3:6), and again at the end of the same list: “And Elishama, and Eliada, and Eliphelet, nine” (1 Chronicles 3:8). The names David gave these sons are confessions — Eliphelet, God is deliverance; Eliada, God knows; Elishama, God has heard. A man who had spent years hunted in caves named his children after what God had proved to be.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) has no entry for Eliphelet; the Hebrew signifies God is deliverance, and the name belongs to sons of David and to one of his mighty men.

expand to see more

ELIPHELET, n. A son of David born in Jerusalem; in Hebrew, God is deliverance.

DELIVERANCE, n. Release from captivity, slavery, oppression or any restraint; rescue from danger.

MIGHTY, a. Very strong; valiant; bold; having great power or physical strength.

COUNSELLOR, n. Any person who gives advice; particularly, one appointed to advise a king or state.

CONFESSION, n. Acknowledgment; the acknowledging of a fault or of the truth; a profession of faith.

Key Scripture

2 Samuel 23:34 — "Eliphelet the son of Ahasbai, the son of the Maachathite, Eliam the son of Ahithophel the Gilonite,"

1 Chronicles 3:6 — "Ibhar also, and Elishama, and Eliphelet,"

1 Chronicles 3:8 — "And Elishama, and Eliada, and Eliphelet, nine."

2 Samuel 11:3 — "And David sent and enquired after the woman. And one said, Is not this Bathsheba, the daughter of Eliam, the wife of Uriah the Hittite?"

Modern Corruption

Naming is treated as a matter of taste, when in Scripture a name is a claim about God or about a circumstance, and the genealogies are full of such claims.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that Hebrew names carry statements. David's Jerusalem-born sons are a small creed read in order: Elishama, God has heard; Eliada, God knows; Eliphelet, God is deliverance. The man who wrote this poor man cried, and the LORD heard him gave his children names that said the same thing every time they were called in to supper. Nathan and Solomon are on the same list, and so is Nathan's line, through which Luke traces the genealogy of Christ.

The mighty-men list carries a different kind of weight. Eliam the son of Ahithophel the Gilonite stands next to Eliphelet in 2 Samuel 23, and 2 Samuel 11:3 identifies Bathsheba as the daughter of Eliam and the wife of Uriah the Hittite — who is himself in the same roll of thirty, a few verses later. The three men most wronged in the Bathsheba affair were all in David's own list of decorated soldiers. Scripture supplies the connection without comment, as it usually does, and leaves the reader to feel what the roll of honour cost.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Eliphelet (H467), God is deliverance; palat (H6403), to escape, deliver; Elishama (H476), God has heard; Elyada (H450), God knows.

expand to see more

Hebrew Eliphelet (H467) — God is deliverance; a son of David and a mighty man.

Hebrew palat (H6403) — to escape, to deliver; the root of the name.

Hebrew Elishama (H476) — God has heard; a brother on the same list.

Hebrew Elyada (H450) — God knows; the third of the confessional names.

Hebrew Achithophel (H302) — Ahithophel; grandfather of Bathsheba, by Eliam.

Usage

"“Eliphelet the son of Ahasbai” — in the roll of the mighty men."

"“Ibhar also, and Elishama, and Eliphelet” — the sons born in Jerusalem."

"“And Elishama, and Eliada, and Eliphelet, nine” — the list closed and counted."
